subject: STABLE step 9: shadow refresh skip by IOSurface seed (render_encoder.inc 25d04271, compositor_submit.inc 3820572e) + per-job bridge cost finding
body: (1) Shadow refresh: tegu_shadow_copy(t,0) now skips lock+full copy when IOSurfaceGetSeed(surface)==seed recorded at the last sync after which the shadow held the surface bytes; the seed is recorded after a read-only refresh (lock seed) and after our own write-back (getSeed after unlock); phase 0 clears it for every shadow a job of the command may write (render target, slots 23..31, v2 writable), so a failed command (no write-back) refreshes again. getSeed is optional (missing symbol = old behaviour). Device evidence that motivates it: TEGU_PERF shadow_kb 1689 per single-command window = ~1.7 MB copied per command. Side effect: replaceRegion/CPU-blit writes into a shadow texture are no longer clobbered by the next refresh while the surface is unchanged (old behaviour lost them). Test async_frontend_test.py (now 6 checks, 39326a6e) FA_SEED: sampled shadow locks per command 1,0,(other writer bumps seed)1,0; shadow render target 2,1,1 (refresh+write-back, then write-back only), shadow bytes == surface every time. Gates: run_host_tests 54 PASS to known stop, CA ASan+release PASS, render harness rc0, integration 1005/2 baseline. (2) FINDING for the render lead (bridge, yours): frame_bench k_* counters show every kernel job costs ALLOC + map + unmap + RELEASE of a fresh command BO (alloc_kib per job: ca200 168 KiB, medium 43 KiB, tick 36 KiB) besides SUBMIT: 4 of the 4 kernel calls per job besides the reap are this churn (kernel_calls/frame = 4 x kjobs with async), plus zero-fill page faults of fresh pages every job. Proposal: a small pool of mapped command BOs per size class (2*N2R_BLOCK and batch multiples) reused once the job that used them is reaped (async: id <= reaped seq; sync: immediately), memset of the used span instead of new pages (check whether n2r_build relies on zeroed memory). Expected: per job -3 IOKit calls and -1 mmap/munmap pair and ~10 page faults; host can show it in frame_bench calls. I can implement it in a separate function if you hand me those draw/batch alloc sites. (3) Our present path: drawables are CA's own (present is CA's); nothing of ours runs there besides the presentation list in teguFinishReport. Backboardd's own CPU cannot be attributed on host; next device run's TEGU_PERF encode_ms vs TEGU_PERF_ENCODE draw_ms gives CA-side time (commit-create minus our draw time).
